title: Setting Up Your Angular Playground 🛠️
description: Install the tools you need and create your first Angular project with the CLI.

slides.title: Tools You Need 🧰
slides.content:
# Prerequisites

Before we code, let’s install two things:

1. **Node.js** (v18+ recommended) – includes npm, the package manager.
2. **Angular CLI** – a command‑line tool that scaffolds, serves, and builds Angular apps.

* Both are free and open source.
* You only need to install them once!

slides.title: Step 1: Install Node.js
slides.content:
Download the LTS version from [nodejs.org](https://nodejs.org) and run the installer.

Verify the installation by opening your terminal and typing:

quizData.question: npm stands for Node _____ Manager.
quizData.explanation: npm is the Node Package Manager, used to install libraries and tools.

slides.title: Step 2: Install Angular CLI
slides.content: Open a terminal and run the following command. The `-g` flag installs it globally so you can use it anywhere.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Verify the CLI Installation

After installation, run `ng version`. You should see a screen with Angular, Node, and OS details. If you get a “command not found” error, try restarting your terminal.

slides.title: Step 3: Create Your First Project
slides.content: Navigate to a folder where you want to keep your code, then generate a new Angular workspace:

slides.title: CLI Options During Setup ⚙️
slides.content:
The CLI will ask two questions:

* **Would you like to add Angular routing?** – for now type `n` (we’ll cover routing in Chapter 5).
* **Which stylesheet format?** – choose **CSS** (the simplest).

Then sit back – the CLI creates all the files and installs dependencies.

quizData.question: Which command creates a new Angular project?
quizData.explanation: `ng new <project-name>` generates a brand new Angular workspace.

slides.title: Project Structure Tour 🗂️
slides.content:
## Important Folders & Files

* `src/app` – where your components live.
* `src/index.html` – the single HTML page that hosts the app.
* `src/main.ts` – the entry point that bootstraps the app.
* `angular.json` – workspace configuration.

We’ll explore `app.component.ts` in the next lesson.
